In what Moses brought, the flesh of camels and the fat of the entrails (thurūb) had been forbidden to them, and He made these lawful for them by the tongue of Jesus; the fats had been forbidden to them, and they were made lawful for them in what Jesus brought; and likewise certain kinds of fish, and certain kinds of birds, those which have no spur (ṣīṣiyah), and other things which He had forbidden them and in which He had been severe upon them; so Jesus came to them with the lightening of that in the Gospel.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Qatādah, the like of it.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Mujāhid, concerning His words and I have come to you with a sign from your Lord (3:50): He said: All the things that Jesus made clear to them, and what his Lord gave him.
### His words, Exalted: Then when Jesus perceived (3:52), the verse

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words Then when Jesus perceived unbelief from them (3:52): He said: They disbelieved and wanted to kill him; that is when he sought the help of his people, and that is when He says: so a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved (61:14).
Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Mujāhid: Who are my helpers unto God? (3:52). He said: Who will follow me unto God?
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Suddī: Who are my helpers unto God? (3:52). He says: with God.
### His words, Exalted: The disciples said (3:52), the verse

Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They were called the disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) only because of the whiteness of their garments; they were fishermen.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Abū Arṭāh, who said: The disciples were the washermen who whiten (yuḥawwirūn) garments, that is, wash them.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples were the washermen; in Nabataean it is hawwārī, and in Arabic, al-muḥawwar (the whitened).
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples were fullers; Jesus passed by them and they believed in him and followed him.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah, who said: The disciples are those who are fit for succession.{{fn:That is, fit to succeed the prophets as their deputies (khilāfah).}}
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: The disciples are the chosen ones (aṣfiyāʾ) of the prophets.
Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The disciples are the chosen ones of the prophets.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah, who said: The ḥawārī is the minister (wazīr).
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, who said: The ḥawārī is the helper.

Al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "Every prophet has a disciple (ḥawārī), and my disciple is al-Zubayr."

Ibn Abī Dāwūd recorded in al-Maṣāḥif, from Asīd ibn Yazīd, who said: "And bear witness that we are Muslims" (wa-shhad bi-annanā muslimūn) (3:52) is in the codex (muṣḥaf) of ʿUthmān in three letters.{{fn:That is, the particle after bi- is written in ʿUthmān's codex in the shorter form of three letters, annā, rather than the fuller annanā.}}
### His words, Exalted: Our Lord, we believe (3:53), the verse

Al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words so write us down among the witnesses (3:53): He said: With Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and his community; for they bore witness for him that he had conveyed the message, and they bore witness for the messengers that they had conveyed it.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, by way of al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: so write us down among the witnesses (3:53). He said: With the Companions of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

Ibn Mardawayh recorded, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say when he had finished his prayer: "O God, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, for those who ask of You have a right upon You, that whatever servant or handmaid among the people of the land and the sea whose call You have accepted and whose supplication You have answered, You make us partners in the good of what they ask of You, and that You grant well-being to us and to them, and accept from us and from them, and pardon us and them; for we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger, so write us down among the witnesses." And he used to say: "No one of His creatures speaks these words but that God makes him a partner in the supplication of the people of their land and the people of their sea, so that it encompasses them all while he remains in his place."

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Suddī, who said: The Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen men of the disciples in a house. Jesus said to his companions: "Who will take on my likeness and be killed, and Paradise shall be his?" One of them took it on, and Jesus was taken up to heaven. That is His words: And they schemed, and God schemed; and God is the best of schemers (3:54).
### His words, Exalted: When God said: O Jesus (3:55), the verse
Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words I am taking you (3:55) (mutawaffīka): He says: I am causing you to die.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: taking you (3:55): from the earth.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by another route, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words I am taking you (3:55): meaning the taking of sleep; God raised him in his sleep. Al-Ḥasan said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the Jews: "Jesus has not died, and he is returning to you before the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Qatādah: I am taking you and raising you to Myself (3:55). He said: This is of the kind in which what comes first is put later and what comes later is put first (al-muqaddam wa-l-muʾakhkhar), that is: raising you to Myself and taking you.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Maṭar al-Warrāq, concerning the verse: He said: Taking you from this world, and it is not the taking of death.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, with a sound chain, from Kaʿb, who said: When Jesus saw the fewness of those who followed him and the multitude of those who denied him, he complained of that to God, and God revealed to him: I am taking you and raising you to Myself (3:55), and one whom I have raised to Myself is not dead; and I shall send you against the one-eyed Dajjāl{{fn:The Dajjāl is the false messiah, or Antichrist, whom Muslim tradition expects at the end of time.}} and you will kill him; then after that you will live twenty-four years; then I shall cause you to die the death of the living. Kaʿb said: And that is the confirmation of the ḥadīth of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) where he said: "How can a community perish of which I am at the beginning and Jesus at the end?"

Isḥāq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: There was no prophet in whose time wonders were more numerous than Jesus, until God raised him. Among the causes of his being raised was that a tyrannical king called Dāwūd ibn Nūdhā, who was the king of the Children of Israel, was the one who sent in search of him to kill him. God had sent down the Gospel to him when he was thirteen years old, and he was raised when he was thirty-four years from his birth. So God revealed to him: I am taking you and raising you to Myself and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55), meaning: and delivering you from the Jews, so that they shall not be able to kill you.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by another route, from al-Ḥasan, concerning the verse: He said: God raised him to Himself, and he is with Him in heaven.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Wahb, who said: God made Jesus son of Mary die for three hours of the day, until He raised him to Himself.
Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Wahb, who said: God made him die for three days, then raised him up and lifted him.

Al-Ḥākim recorded, from Wahb, that God made Jesus die for seven hours, then brought him to life; and that Mary conceived him when she was thirteen years old; and that he was raised at the age of thirty-three; and that his mother remained six years after he was raised.

Isḥāq ibn Bishr and Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, by way of Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words I am taking you and raising you (3:55): meaning raising you, then taking you at the end of time.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning the verse: He said: His raising him is His taking him.

Al-Ḥākim recorded, from al-Ḥurayth ibn Makhashsh, that ʿAlī was killed on the morning of the twenty-first of Ramaḍān, "and I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī saying: He was killed on the night the Qurʾān was sent down, the night Jesus was taken up by night, and the night Moses was taken."
Ibn Saʿd, Aḥmad in al-Zuhd and al-Ḥākim recorded, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Jesus was raised at the age of thirty-three years, and Muʿādh died at that same age.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55): He said: He purified him from the Jews, the Christians and the Magians, and from the unbelievers of his people.
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: and purifying you from those who disbelieve (3:55). He said: When they intended against you what they intended.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Qatādah, concerning His words and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55): He said: They are the people of Islam, who followed him upon his natural disposition (fiṭrah), his religion and his way; they shall not cease to prevail over those who oppose them until the Day of Resurrection.
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning the verse: He said: Giving victory to those who follow you in Islam over those who disbelieve, until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "A party of my community shall not cease to prevail, not caring who opposes them, until the command of God comes." Al-Nuʿmān said: So whoever says that I am attributing to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) what he did not say, the confirmation of this is in the Book of God, Exalted; God, Exalted, said: and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55), the verse.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan: and placing those who follow you (3:55). He said: They are the Muslims, and we are of them, and we are above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "A band of my community shall never cease to fight for the truth, prevailing over the people, until the command of God comes while they are upon that." Then he drew upon this verse: O Jesus, I am taking you and raising you to Myself and purifying you from those who disbelieve and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection (3:55).

Ibn Jarīr recorded, from Ibn Zayd, concerning the verse: He said: The Christians are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection; there is no land in which there is any of the Christians but that they are above the Jews, in east or west; the Jews are humbled in all lands.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded, from al-Ḥasan, concerning the verse: He said: Jesus is raised up with God, then he will descend before the Day of Resurrection; and whoever believes in Jesus and in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and is upon their religion, they shall not cease to prevail over those who part from them until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Jarīr recorded, by way of ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds (3:57): He says: who perform My obligations; He will pay them their rewards in full (3:57): He says: He will give them the recompense of their righteous deeds complete, nothing of it being withheld from them, nor will they diminish it.
### His words, Exalted: This We recite to you (3:58), the verse

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The two monks of Najrān came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and one of them said: "Who is the father of Jesus?" The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would not hasten until he had consulted his Lord, and there came down to him: This We recite to you of the signs and the wise Remembrance (3:58), up to His words: of the doubters (3:60).
Ibn Jarīr recorded, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning His words and the wise Remembrance (3:58): He said: The Qurʾān.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, from ʿAlī: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "There will be trials (fitan)." I said: "What is the way out of them?" He said: "The Book of God; it is the wise Remembrance and the straight path."
His words, Exalted: Surely the likeness of Jesus (3:59), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that a group of the people of Najrān{{fn:a Christian town and district in the south of Arabia, whose delegation came to the Prophet in Medina}} came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and among them were al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib{{fn:the two leading men of the Christian delegation of Najrān: al-Sayyid was their chief and al-ʿĀqib his deputy and the holder of their counsel}}. They said to him: “What is it with you, that you speak of our companion?” He said: “Who is he?” They said: “Jesus; you claim that he is the servant of God!” He said: “Indeed, he is the servant of God.” They said: “Have you ever seen the like of Jesus, or been told of one?” Then they went out from his presence, and Gabriel came to him and said: Say to them when they come to you: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), to the end of the verse.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the two lords of the people of Najrān and their two bishops, al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib, met the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and asked him about Jesus. They said: “Every son of Adam has a father; so what is the case of Jesus, who has no father?” So God sent down concerning him this verse: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God (3:59), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr recorded from al-Suddī, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent and the people of Najrān heard of him, four men from among the best of them came to him, among them al-ʿĀqib, al-Sayyid, Māsarjis and Mārbaḥr. They asked him what he said about Jesus. He said: “He is the servant of God, and His spirit, and His word.” They said: “No; rather he is God, who came down from His kingdom and entered into the womb of Mary, then came forth from her, and so showed us His power and His command. Have you ever seen a human being created without a father?” So God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿIkrimah concerning His words: Surely the likeness of Jesus (3:59), the verse. He said: It was sent down concerning al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid of the people of Najrān.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj, who said: It has reached us that the Christians of Najrān sent their delegation to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), among them al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib, who at that time were the two lords of the people of Najrān. They said: “O Muḥammad, why do you revile our companion?” He said: “Who is your companion?” They said: “Jesus son of Mary; you claim that he is a servant.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Indeed, he is the servant of God and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him.” They grew angry and said: “If you are truthful, then show us a servant who gives life to the dead, heals the blind from birth, and creates from clay the likeness of a bird and breathes into it”—the verse—“No, rather he is God.” He kept silent until Gabriel came to him and said: “O Muḥammad, They have certainly disbelieved who say that God is the Messiah, son of Mary (5:17), the verse.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “O Gabriel, they asked me to tell them of the likeness of Jesus.” Gabriel said: The likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him “Be”, and he was.
When morning came they returned, and he recited the verses to them.

Ibn Saʿd and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded from al-Azraq ibn Qays, who said: The bishop of Najrān and al-ʿĀqib came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he offered Islam to them. They said: “We were already Muslims before you.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “You both lie. Three things keep you from Islam: your saying that God has taken a son, your prostration to the cross, and your eating the flesh of swine.” They said: “Then who is the father of Jesus?” He did not know what to say, and so God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), up to His words the corrupters (3:63). When these verses came down, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called the two of them to mutual imprecation (mulāʿanah){{fn:the solemn procedure of 3:61 in which each party calls down the curse of God upon whichever of them is lying; also called mubāhalah}}, and they said: “If he is a prophet, it is not fitting for us to imprecate against him.” So they refused, and said: “Do you offer anything other than this?” He said: “Islam, or the poll-tax (jizyah), or war.” So they agreed to the poll-tax.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters (3:60), meaning: do not be in doubt concerning Jesus, that he is as the likeness of Adam—the servant of God, His messenger and His word.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The delegation of Najrān came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “Tell us about Jesus son of Mary.” He said: “The messenger of God and His word which He cast to Mary.” They said: “Jesus ought to be above this.” So God sent down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), the verse. They said: “Jesus ought not to be like Adam.” So God sent down: So whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you (3:61), the verse.

Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Would that there were a veil between me and the people of Najrān, so that I should not see them and they should not see me”—because of the severity with which they used to dispute with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

Al-Bayhaqī recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of Salamah ibn ʿAbd Yashūʿ, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote to the people of Najrān, before Ṭā Sīn Sulaymān{{fn:that is, Sūrat al-Naml (27), which opens with the letters Ṭā Sīn and contains Solomon's letter beginning “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful” (27:30); before it was revealed the Prophet's letters opened with the older formula “In the name of the God of…” or “In Your name, O God”}} was sent down to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), to the bishop of Najrān and the people of Najrān. If you submit, then I praise to you God, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. To proceed: I call you to the worship of God rather than the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God rather than the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then the poll-tax; and if you refuse that, then I have given you notice of war. And peace.” When the bishop read the letter he was appalled by it and seized with a great dread, and he sent for a man of the people of Najrān called Shuraḥbīl ibn Wadāʿah and handed him the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He read it, and the bishop said to him: “What is your view?” Shuraḥbīl said: “You know what God promised Abraham concerning prophethood among the descendants of Ishmael; so what is to guarantee that this is not that man? I have no opinion to give on prophethood; were it a matter of worldly affairs I would counsel you in it and strive on your behalf.” The bishop then sent for one man after another of the people of Najrān, and every one of them said the same as Shuraḥbīl had said. So their opinion was agreed that they should send Shuraḥbīl ibn Wadāʿah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shuraḥbīl and Jabbār ibn Fayḍ, to bring them back news of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The delegation set out until they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); he questioned them and they questioned him, and the questioning went on between him and them until they said to him: “What do you say about Jesus son of Mary?” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “I have nothing on him this day of mine; so stay until I inform you of what is told me concerning Jesus tomorrow morning.” Then God sent down this verse: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam (3:59), up to His words: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61). They refused to acknowledge that, and when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) rose the next morning, after he had told them the news, he came forward wrapping al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn in a cloak of his, with Fāṭimah walking behind his back, for the mutual imprecation; and he had at that time a number of wives. Shuraḥbīl said to his two companions: “I see a matter coming upon us. If this man is a prophet sent by God and we imprecate against him, there will not remain on the face of the earth of us a hair or a nail but it will perish.” They said to him: “What is your view?” He said: “My view is that I should let him be the judge over us, for I see a man who will never judge unjustly.” They said to him: “It is yours to decide.” Shuraḥbīl went to meet the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “I have seen something better than imprecating against you.” He said: “And what is it?” He said: “Your judgement, this day until nightfall and your night until the morning; whatever you judge concerning us is binding.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) went back and did not imprecate against them, and made peace with them on terms of the poll-tax.

Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Ḥudhayfah that al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he wished to imprecate against them, but one of them said to his companion: “Do not imprecate against him, for by God, if he is a prophet and he imprecates against us, neither we nor our posterity after us will ever prosper.” So they said to him: “We will give you what you have asked; so send with us a trustworthy man.” He said: “Rise, O Abū ʿUbaydah.” And when he stood up he said: “This is the trustee of this community.”

Al-Ḥākim—who declared it sound—Ibn Mardawayh and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Jābir, who said: Al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he called them to Islam. They said: “We have submitted, O Muḥammad.”

He said: “You both lie. If you wish, I shall tell you what keeps you from Islam.” They said: “Go on, then.” He said: “Love of the cross, drinking of wine, and eating the flesh of swine.” Jābir said: Then he called them to mutual imprecation, and they made an appointment with him for the morrow. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) went out in the morning and took ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn by the hand, then sent for the two of them; but they refused to answer him and yielded to him. He said: “By Him who sent me with the truth, had they done it, the valley would have rained fire upon them.” Jābir said: Concerning them was sent down: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the verse. Jābir said: and ourselves and yourselves (3:61): the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and ʿAlī; our sons (3:61): al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn; and our women (3:61): Fāṭimah.

Al-Ḥākim—who declared it sound—recorded from Jābir that the delegation of Najrān came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “What do you say about Jesus?” He said: “He is the spirit of God and His word, and the servant of God and His messenger.” They said to him: “Are you willing that we should imprecate with you that it is not so?” He said: “Is that more pleasing to you?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “Then whenever you wish.” He came and gathered his offspring, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and their chief said: “Do not imprecate against this man, for by God, if you imprecate against him, one of the two parties will surely be swallowed up by the earth.” So they came and said: “O Abū al-Qāsim, it was only our foolish ones who wished to imprecate against you, and we would like you to excuse us.” He said: “I have excused you.” Then he said: “The punishment had overshadowed Najrān.”

Abū Nuʿaym recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the delegation of Najrān, of the Christians, came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), fourteen men of their nobles, among them al-Sayyid, who was the great one among them, and al-ʿĀqib, who was the one next after him and the holder of their counsel. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the two of them: “Submit.” They said: “We have submitted.” He said: “You have not submitted.” They said: “Yes indeed, we submitted before you.” He said: “You both lie. Three things in you keep you from Islam: your worship of the cross, your eating of swine, and your claim that God has a son.” And there came down: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust (3:59), the verse. When he recited it to them they said: “We do not recognise what you say.” And there came down: So whoever disputes with you concerning him after the knowledge that has come to you (3:61). He says: whoever argues with you about the matter of Jesus after there has come to you of the knowledge (3:61)—of the Qurʾān—then say: Come (3:61), up to His words: then let us earnestly pray (3:61). He says: let us strive in supplication that what Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) has brought is the truth and that what they say is falsehood. He said to them: “God has commanded me, if you do not accept this, to engage you in mutual imprecation (mubāhalah).” They said: “O Abū al-Qāsim, rather let us go back and consider our affair, then we will come to you.” They withdrew with one another and spoke frankly among themselves. Al-Sayyid said to al-ʿĀqib: “By God, you know that the man is a prophet sent by God, and if you imprecate against him it will mean your extirpation; never did a people imprecate against a prophet and their elder survive or their young one grow up. So if you will not follow him and insist only on clinging to your religion, then make a truce with him and return to your country.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had gone out with ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and Fāṭimah with him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “When I pray, say Amen.” But they refused to imprecate against him and made peace with him on terms of the poll-tax.

Abū Nuʿaym recorded in al-Dalāʾil, by way of ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that eight of the bishops of the Arabs, of the people of Najrān, came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), among them al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid. So God sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), up to His words: then let us earnestly pray (3:61). He means: let us call upon God to lay the curse upon the liar. They said: “Grant us a delay of three days.” So they went to Banū Qurayẓah, al-Naḍīr and Banū Qaynuqāʿ{{fn:the three Jewish tribes of Medina}} and consulted them, and these counselled them to make peace with him and not to imprecate against him, for he was the prophet whom we find in the Torah. So they made peace with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on terms of a thousand garments in Ṣafar and a thousand in Rajab, and dirhams.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Qatādah: So whoever disputes with you concerning him (3:61): concerning Jesus; then say: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), the verse. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) summoned the delegation of Najrān to this, and they are the ones who had disputed with him concerning Jesus; but they drew back and refused. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Punishment had indeed come down upon the people of Najrān; had they done it, they would have been extirpated from the face of the earth.”

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū Nuʿaym recorded from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The people of Najrān were the most extreme of the Christians in what they said about Jesus son of Mary, and they used to argue with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about him. So God sent down these verses in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: Surely the likeness of Jesus with God (3:59), up to His words: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61). He was commanded to engage them in mutual imprecation, and they made an appointment with him for the morrow. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) went out in the morning with al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and Fāṭimah with him; but they refused to imprecate against him and made peace with him on terms of the poll-tax. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The bearer of tidings came to me with the destruction of the people of Najrān, even to the birds upon the trees, had they gone through with the mutual imprecation.”

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Bukhārī, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Mardawayh and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Dalāʾil recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Had the people of Najrān engaged in mutual imprecation with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), they would have returned to find neither family nor property.

Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, who said: When this verse was sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, and said: “O God, these are my family.”

Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿAlbāʾ ibn Aḥmar al-Yashkurī, who said: When this verse was sent down: then say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons (3:61), the verse, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent for ʿAlī, Fāṭimah and their two sons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and summoned the Jews to imprecate against them. A young man of the Jews said: “Woe to you! Is it not within your recent memory, as of yesterday, that your brethren were transformed into apes and swine? Do not imprecate.” So they desisted.

Ibn ʿAsākir recorded from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, concerning this verse: Come, let us call our sons (3:61), the verse. He said: He brought Abū Bakr and his son, ʿUmar and his son, ʿUthmān and his son, and ʿAlī and his son.
Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded, by way of Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn ʿAbbās: then let us earnestly pray (3:61): let us strive in supplication.

Al-Ḥākim—who declared it sound—and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “This is sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ),” pointing with the finger next to the thumb; “and this is supplication (duʿāʾ),” and he raised his hands level with his shoulders; “and this is earnest entreaty (ibtihāl),” and he raised his hands stretched out high.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās: Surely this is the true narrative (3:62). He says: surely this which We have said concerning Jesus is the truth.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd recorded from Qays ibn Saʿd, who said: There was something between Ibn ʿAbbās and another man, and he recited this verse: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us earnestly pray (3:61), and he raised his hands and faced the Corner{{fn:the corner of the Kaʿbah in which the Black Stone is set}}: and invoke the curse of God upon the liars (3:61).
His words, Exalted: Say: O People of the Book, come (3:64), the verse.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite in the two rakʿahs of dawn, in the first of them: Say: We believe in God and what has been sent down to us (2:136), the verse; and in the second: Come to a word common between us and you (3:64).

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Abū Sufyān related to me that Heraclius called for the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and read it, and in it was: “In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: I call you with the summons of Islam. Submit, and you will be safe; submit, and God will give you your reward twice over. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the arīsiyyīn{{fn:the peasants or subject tillers of the land under Byzantine rule; the sin of their remaining outside Islam would fall upon Heraclius if he turned them away from it}}. O People of the Book, come to a word common between us and you: that we worship none but God, and that we associate nothing with Him (3:64),” up to His words: bear witness that we are Muslims (3:64).

Al-Ṭabarānī recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to the unbelievers was: Come to a word common between us and you (3:64), to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: Come to a word (3:64), the verse. He said: It has reached me that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews of the people of Medina to that, but they refused him; so he fought them until they agreed to the poll-tax (jizyah).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews of the people of Medina to the common word; they are the ones who disputed concerning Abraham and claimed that he died a Jew, so God gave them the lie and disowned them from him, saying: O People of the Book, why do you dispute concerning Abraham (3:65), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr recorded from al-Rabīʿ, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) called the Jews to the common word.

He recorded from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr concerning His words: Say: O People of the Book, come (3:64), the verse. He said: So he called them to a fair settlement and cut off the argument from them—meaning the delegation of Najrān.

He recorded from al-Suddī, who said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called them—meaning the delegation of the Christians of Najrān—and said: O People of the Book, come to a common word (3:64), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Qatādah: Come to a word common (3:64). He said: just.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded the like of it from al-Rabīʿ.

Al-Ṭastī recorded in his Masāʾil{{fn:the “Questions of Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq”, a collection of lexical questions put to Ibn ʿAbbās, each answered with a verse of Arabic poetry}} from Ibn ʿAbbās that Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq asked him about His words: common between us and you (3:64). He said: just. He said: And do the Arabs know that? He said: Yes; have you not heard the words of the poet:
> We met and settled our account on even terms (sawāʾ), but he was dragged from one state to another.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, who said: The common word is: there is no god but God.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Mujāhid: Come to a word common (3:64). He said: there is no god but God.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: and that none of us take others as lords apart from God (3:64). He said: that none of us obey another in disobedience to God. And it is said that that lordship consists in people obeying their chiefs and leaders in what is not worship, even though they do not pray to them.
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from ʿIkrimah concerning His words: and that none of us take others as lords (3:64). He said: their prostrating to one another.
His words, Exalted: The People of the Book ask you (4:153), the verses.

Ibn Jarīr recorded from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, who said: Some people of the Jews came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: “Moses brought us the tablets from God; so bring us tablets from God, that we may believe you.” So God sent down: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven (4:153), up to His words: and their uttering against Mary a monstrous calumny (4:156).

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning the verse. He said: The Jews and the Christians said to Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): “We will never pledge allegiance to you on what you call us to until you bring us a book from God: from God to so-and-so, that you are the Messenger of God; and to so-and-so, that you are the Messenger of God.” So God sent down: The People of the Book ask you (4:153), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr recorded from al-Suddī concerning the verse. He said: The Jews said: “If you are truthful that you are the Messenger of God, then bring us a book written from heaven, as Moses brought it.”

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Qatādah concerning His words: to bring down to them a book from heaven (4:153), that is, a book for them in particular; and concerning His words: openly (4:153), that is, in plain sight.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: and they said: Show us God openly (4:153). He said: Had they seen Him, they would simply have seen Him; what they said, openly, was: “Show us God.” He said: it is a case of what is placed first belonging later and what is placed later belonging first (muqaddam wa-muʾakhkhar){{fn:that is, Ibn ʿAbbās takes “openly” to qualify their saying, not the seeing: “they said openly: Show us God”}}.

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr recorded from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he recited: so the thunderbolt (al-ṣaʿqah) seized them{{fn:a variant reading (qirāʾah) of 4:153, al-ṣaʿqah in place of the standard al-ṣāʿiqah}}.

Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: so the thunderbolt seized them (4:153). He said: Death; God made them die before their appointed terms, as a punishment for what they said, for as long as God willed to keep them dead; then He raised them up.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Qatādah: and We raised the Mount above them (4:154). He said: a mountain at whose foot they were; God lifted it and set it above them as though it were a canopy, and said: “You shall take My command, or I shall cast it upon you.” They said: “We take it.” So God held it back from them.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir recorded from Qatādah concerning His words: and We said to them: Enter the gate prostrating (4:154). He said: We used to be told that it was one of the gates of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). And We said to them: Do not transgress on the Sabbath (4:154). He said: He commanded the people not to eat fish on the Sabbath day and not to interfere with them, and whatever was besides that was made lawful to them. And concerning His words: So for their breaking (4:155), He says: for their breaking of their covenant; and their saying: Our hearts are wrapped (4:155), that is, they do not understand; rather God has set a seal upon them (4:155), He says: when the people abandoned God's command, killed His messengers, disbelieved in His signs and broke the covenant that was upon them, God set a seal upon their hearts and cursed them when they did that.

Al-Bazzār, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Shuʿab{{fn:Shuʿab al-īmān, “The Branches of Faith”}}—who declared it weak—recorded from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: “The seal hangs from a leg of the Throne; when what is sacred is violated, and sins are committed, and insolence is shown towards God, God sends the seal and it seals his heart, and after that he accepts nothing.”
Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: and their uttering against Mary a monstrous calumny (4:156). He said: they accused her of fornication.

Al-Bukhārī in his Tārīkh, and al-Ḥākim—who declared it sound—recorded from ʿAlī, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: “In you there is a likeness to Jesus: the Jews hated him until they slandered his mother, and the Christians loved him until they set him in a station that is not his.”
His words, Exalted: And God is ever Mighty, Wise (4:158).
Ibn Jarīr recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: And God is ever Mighty, Wise (4:158). He said: the meaning of that is that He is so.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim recorded from Ibn ʿAbbās that a Jew said to him: “You claim that God was Mighty, Wise; so how is He today?” Ibn ʿAbbās said: “He was Mighty, Wise in Himself.”{{fn:the Jew's objection turns on the past tense of kāna, “was”; Ibn ʿAbbās answers that these are attributes God has of Himself, not ones He acquired or lost}}
### His words, Exalted: When God said: O Jesus son of Mary (5:110), the verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsākir reported from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the prophets and their communities will be summoned; then Jesus will be summoned, and God will remind him of His favour upon him, and he will acknowledge it. He will say: O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother (5:110), the verse. Then He will say: Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? (5:116). He will deny having said that. Then the Christians will be brought and questioned, and they will say: Yes, he commanded us to do that. Then the hair of Jesus will grow long, until every angel among the angels takes hold of a hair from the hair of his head and his body, and he will kneel in dispute with them before God for the measure of a thousand years, until he establishes the proof against them, the cross is raised up before them, and they are taken off to the Fire."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported by way of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Ibn Wahb, from his father, who said: A man of the People of the Book came to Yemen, and my father said: Go to him and hear from him. I said: Are you sending me off to a Christian man? He said: Yes, go to him and hear from him. So I went to him, and he said: When God raised up Jesus (peace be upon him), He stood him before Gabriel and Michael and said to him: Remember My favour upon you and upon your mother. I did such and such for you, and such and such; then I brought you forth from your mother's womb, and I did such and such for you, and such and such. And there will be a community after you who will lay claim to you and lay claim to your lordship, and will testify that you have died—and how can there be a Lord who dies? By My might I have sworn: I shall surely bring them to account on the Day of Resurrection, and I shall surely set them in the station of a litigant facing his litigant, until they make good what they said—and they will never make it good. Then that man accepted Islam, and he brought reports the like of which I had never heard.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words: and when I restrained the Children of Israel from you, when you came to them with the clear proofs (5:110): that is, the signs which He placed in his hands—the raising of the dead; his making from clay the likeness of a bird, then breathing into it so that it became a bird by God's leave; the healing of sicknesses; and the telling of many unseen things, such as what they stored up in their houses—and what he restored to them of the Torah, together with the Gospel which God newly sent down to him. Then He mentioned their disbelief in all of that.
### His words, Exalted: And when I inspired (5:111), the verse.
Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh reported from al-Suddī concerning His words: And when I inspired the disciples (5:111): he says: I cast it into their hearts.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported from Qatādah: And when I inspired the disciples (5:111): he said: an inspiration (waḥy) cast into their hearts, not the inspiration of prophethood. Inspiration is of two kinds: an inspiration which the angels bring, and an inspiration which is cast into the heart of the servant.
### His words, Exalted: When the disciples said (5:112) — the verses.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her), who said: The disciples knew God too well to say, "Is your Lord able?" They only said, "Are you able to ask your Lord — are you able to call upon Him?"

Al-Ḥākim — who declared it sound — al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm, who said: I asked Muʿādh ibn Jabal about the saying of the disciples, Is your Lord able (hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka), or "Are you able to ask your Lord" (hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka)? He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) taught me to recite it hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka, with the tāʾ.
Abū ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he recited it hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka, with the tāʾ and with rabbaka in the accusative.
Abū ʿUbayd and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he recited it hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka, and said: "Are you able to ask your Lord?"

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī that ʿAlī used to recite it Is your Lord able (hal yastaṭīʿu rabbuka); he said: Will your Lord respond to you?{{fn:The gloss reads hal yuṭīʿuka rabbuka, taking istaṭāʿa in the sense of aṭāʿa, "to comply with, to answer".}}
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmitted from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Abū Rajāʾ that the two of them recited Is your Lord able, with the yāʾ and the nominative.

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words Is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven (5:112): he said: They said, "Will your Lord respond to you if you ask Him?" So God sent down to them a table from heaven, on which was every kind of food except meat, and they ate from it.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning His words a table (māʾidah): he said: The māʾidah is the khiwān{{fn:A tray or low table on which food is set out.}}; and concerning His words and that may be at rest (5:113): he said: that may be certain.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us (5:114): he says: We shall take the day on which it came down as a festival, which we and those after us shall hold in honour.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Qatādah concerning His words that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us: he said: They wanted it to be for their descendants after them.

Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī in Nawādir al-uṣūl, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh in al-ʿAẓamah, and Abū Bakr al-Shāfiʿī in his Fawāʾid known as al-Ghaylāniyyāt transmitted from Salmān al-Fārisī, who said: When the disciples asked Jesus son of Mary for the table, he disliked that intensely, and said: "Be content with what God has provided you on the earth, and do not ask for the table from heaven; for if it comes down to you it will be a sign from your Lord, and Thamūd perished only when they asked their prophet for a sign and were tried by it, until their destruction lay in it." But they would accept nothing except that he bring it to them, and for that reason they said: We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses (5:113). When Jesus saw that they would accept nothing but that he pray to God for it on their behalf, he stood up, cast off his wool and put on black hair-cloth, a tunic of hair and a cloak of hair; then he performed the ablution, bathed, entered his place of prayer and prayed as long as God willed. When he had finished his prayer he stood upright facing the qiblah, set his feet side by side until they were even, placing heel against heel and toe against toe, laid his right hand upon his left over his chest, lowered his gaze and bowed his head in humility. Then he let loose his eyes in weeping, and his tears did not cease to flow down his cheeks and drip from the ends of his beard, until the ground before his face was wet from his humility. When he saw that, he called upon God and said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us (5:114) — that it may be an admonition from You to us — and a sign from You, that is, a token from You which shall be between us and You; and provide us upon it food that we may eat, and You are the best of providers. So God sent down to them a red cloth (sufrah) between two clouds, a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they watched it in the air plunging down from the sphere of heaven and descending towards them; and Jesus wept for fear of the conditions which God had laid upon them concerning it: that He would punish whoever among them disbelieved in it after it had come down with a punishment with which He had not punished anyone in all the worlds. And he was praying to God in his place, saying: "My God, make it a mercy; my God, do not make it a punishment; my God, how many a wondrous thing have I asked of You, and You have granted me; my God, make us thankful to You; my God, I seek refuge in You lest You should have sent it down in anger and as a scourge; my God, make it safety and well-being, and do not make it a trial and an exemplary punishment." He did not cease praying until the cloth settled before Jesus, with the disciples and his companions around him, and they smelled a sweet fragrance the like of which they had never smelled before. Jesus and the disciples fell down prostrate to God in thanks to Him for what He had provided them from where they had not reckoned, and for having shown them in it a mighty sign full of wonder and admonition. The Jews came to look, and they saw a wondrous thing which left them in grief and distress, and then they went away in great rage. Jesus, the disciples and his companions came forward and sat down around the cloth, and behold, over it was a napkin covering it. Jesus said: "Which of us is boldest to lift the napkin from this cloth, most confident in himself and best in his standing with his Lord? Let him uncover this sign, that we may see it, praise our Lord, mention His name and eat of His provision which He has provided us." The disciples said: "O Spirit of God and His Word, you are the worthiest of us for that, and the one most entitled among us to uncover it." So Jesus arose and performed a fresh ablution, then entered his place of prayer and prayed some units of prayer (rakaʿāt) for that, then wept for a long time and prayed to God to permit him to uncover it and to place in it blessing and provision for him and for his people. Then he went and sat down at the cloth, took hold of the napkin and said: "In the name of God, the best of providers," and uncovered the cloth; and behold, upon it was a huge roasted fish, with no scales upon it and no bones in its belly, from which fat flowed in a stream. Around it were arranged vegetables of every kind except leeks; at its head was vinegar and at its tail salt; and around the vegetables were five loaves, on one of which were olives, on another fruits, and on another five pomegranates. Simon, the head of the disciples, said to Jesus: "O Spirit of God and His Word, is this of the food of this world or of the food of Paradise?" He said: "Is it not time for you to take warning from the signs you see, and to desist from prying into questions? How I fear for you that you will be punished on account of this sign!" Simon said: "No, by the God of Israel, I intended no evil by it, O son of the Truthful One (al-Ṣiddīqah)." Jesus said: "Nothing of what you see upon it is of the food of Paradise, nor of the food of this world; it is only something God originated in the air by overwhelming, all-subduing power. He said to it, 'Be,' and it was, quicker than the blink of an eye. So eat of what you asked for, in the name of God, and praise your Lord for it, and He will supply you more of it and increase you; for He is Originator, All-Powerful, Appreciative." They said: "O Spirit of God and His Word, we should love for you to show us a sign within this sign." Jesus said: "Glory be to God! Were you not satisfied with what you have seen of this sign, that you should ask for yet another sign within it?" Then Jesus turned to the fish and said: "O fish, return, by God's leave, alive as you were." And God brought it to life by His power, and it quivered and returned, by God's leave, alive and fresh, licking its lips as a lion licks its lips, its eyes rolling with a gleam in them, and its scales returned upon it. The people took fright at it and shrank back. When Jesus saw that from them, he said: "What is the matter with you? You ask for a sign, and when your Lord shows it to you, you loathe it. How I fear for you that you will be punished for what you are doing! O fish, return, by God's leave, as you were." And it returned, by God's leave, roasted as it had been in its first created state. They said to Jesus: "O Spirit of God, be the one who begins eating from it, and then we after you." He said: "God forbid that! Let him who asked for it begin eating." When the disciples and their companions saw their prophet's refusal to eat of it, they feared that its descent was out of displeasure and that in eating of it lay an exemplary punishment, so they kept away from it. When Jesus saw that, he called to it the poor and the chronically ill, and said: "Eat of your Lord's provision and the invocation of your prophet, and praise God who sent it down for you; its benefit shall be yours and its punishment upon others. Open your eating with the name of God and close it with praise of God." They did so, and one thousand three hundred people ate from it, men and women alike, each of them going away from it full and belching. Jesus and the disciples looked, and behold, what was on it was just as it had been when it came down from heaven, nothing diminished from it. Then it was raised up to heaven while they watched. Every poor person who ate from it became rich, and every chronically ill person among them who ate from it was cured, and they remained rich and healthy until they departed this world. The disciples and their companions who had refused to eat from it felt a remorse that made their eyelids run with tears, and the regret of it remained in their hearts until the day of death. He said: Thereafter, whenever the table came down, the Children of Israel came hastening to it from every place, jostling one another — rich and poor, women, young and old, healthy and sick — climbing over one another. When Jesus saw that, he made it come in turns among them, so that it came down one day and not the next. They remained in that state for forty days, it coming down to them on alternate days when the forenoon was high, and it would remain set out, being eaten from, until, when they declared themselves done, it was raised from them, by God's leave, into the air of the sky, while they watched its shadow on the earth until it disappeared from them.

Then God revealed to Jesus: "Make My provision in the table for the orphans, the poor and the chronically ill, to the exclusion of the rich among the people." When God did that, the rich grew doubtful of it and disparaged it, until they doubted it within themselves and made the people doubt it, and spread abroad foul and reprehensible talk about it. Satan obtained from them what he wanted, and cast his whispering into the hearts of the doubters until they said to Jesus: "Tell us about the table: is its coming down from heaven true? For many a man among us has come to doubt it." Jesus said: "You have perished, by the God of the Messiah! You asked your prophet for the table, that he should seek it for you from your Lord; and when he did so, and God sent it down to you as mercy and provision and showed you in it signs and lessons, you called it a lie and doubted it. So receive tidings of punishment, for it is coming down upon you, unless God has mercy on you." And God revealed to Jesus: "I am taking the deniers according to My condition: I shall punish whoever among them disbelieves in the table after it has come down with a punishment with which I punish no one in all the worlds." So when the doubters in it came to the evening and took to their beds, in the finest of forms, with their wives, secure, then in the last part of the night God transformed them into swine, and in the morning they were rooting after filth in the rubbish-heaps.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to relate of Jesus son of Mary that he said to the Children of Israel: "Will you fast to God for thirty days, then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the wage of the labourer is owed by him for whom he laboured." They did so, then said: "O teacher of goodness, you told us that the wage of the labourer is owed by him for whom he laboured, and you commanded us to fast thirty days, and we did; and we never worked thirty days for anyone without his feeding us. So is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven" — up to His words anyone in all the worlds (5:112–115). Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven, upon it seven fish and seven loaves, until they set it down before them, and the last of the people ate from it as the first of them had eaten.

Al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn al-Anbārī in Kitāb al-Aḍdād, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The table was sent down from heaven as bread and meat, and they were commanded not to be unfaithful and not to store up for the morrow; but they were unfaithful, and stored up, and put away for the morrow, and so they were transformed into apes and swine."
Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted, by another route, from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, as a halted report (mawqūf), the like of it. Al-Tirmidhī said: And the halted version is the sounder.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: The table came down with fruit of the fruit of Paradise upon it.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The table was a fish and loaves.

Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah transmitted from ʿIkrimah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Were it not for the Children of Israel, bread would not go stale nor meat go rotten; but they hid it away for the morrow, so the meat went rotten and the bread went stale."
Ibn al-Anbārī in Kitāb al-Aḍdād transmitted from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven (5:114): he said: bread and fish.

Ibn al-Anbārī, and Abū al-Shaykh in al-ʿAẓamah, transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: The table came down, and it was food that steamed hot, and they used to eat from it sitting; then they did wrong, and it was raised a little, so they ate on their knees; then they did wrong, and it was raised a little, so they ate standing; then they did wrong, and it was raised altogether.

Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: It was a table at which four thousand would sit. They said of a group of their lowly folk: "These people are soiling our clothes upon us; if only we built a platform for it to raise it up." So they built a platform for it, and the weak could no longer reach anything. When they contravened the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, He raised it from them.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn al-Anbārī in Kitāb al-Aḍdād and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, who said: The table was a fish in which was the taste of every food.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from ʿIkrimah that the bread which was sent down with the table was of rice.

Ibn Jarīr transmitted, by way of al-ʿAwfī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: There came down to Jesus son of Mary and the disciples a tray on which were bread and fish, from which they would eat wherever they alighted, whenever they wished.
Ibn Jarīr, and Ibn al-Anbārī in Kitāb al-Aḍdād, transmitted by way of ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning the table: he said: It was food that came down to them from heaven wherever they alighted.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Mujāhid, who said: It is the food that came down to them wherever they alighted.

Ibn Jarīr transmitted from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the table came down to Jesus son of Mary with seven loaves and seven fish upon it, from which they ate whatever they wished; then some of them stole from it, saying, "Perhaps it will not come down tomorrow," and so it was raised.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Anbārī and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that it was a table on which fruit of the fruits of Paradise came down, and they were commanded not to hide away, not to be unfaithful and not to store up for the morrow — a trial with which God tried them; and whenever they did any of that, Jesus would inform them of it. But the people were unfaithful in it, and hid away and stored up for the morrow.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: Everything was sent down upon the table except meat; and the māʾidah is the khiwān.

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Maysarah and Zādhān, who both said: Whenever the table was set for the Children of Israel, hands went back and forth upon it among every kind of food.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he was asked about the table which God sent down from heaven to the Children of Israel, and he said: There came down to them every day, on that table, some of the fruits of Paradise, and they ate what they wished of various kinds; four thousand would sit at it, and when they had eaten, God replaced it with the like of it, and they continued thus as long as God willed.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Mujāhid concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven: he said: It is a parable that was struck, and nothing came down to them.

Abū ʿUbayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Mujāhid, who said: A table with food upon it; they refused it when the punishment was presented to them should they disbelieve, so they refused to have it come down to them.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn al-Anbārī transmitted from al-Ḥasan, who said: When it was said to them but whoever of you disbelieves thereafter, I shall punish him with a punishment (5:115), they said: "We have no need of it," and so it did not come down to them.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah concerning His words I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one in all the worlds (5:115): he said: It was mentioned to us that when they did with the table what they did, they were turned into swine.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words but whoever of you disbelieves thereafter — after the table had come to him — I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one in all the worlds: he says: I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one other than the people of the table.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those of the people of the table who disbelieved, the hypocrites, and the house of Pharaoh.
ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmitted from ʿĀṣim that he recited I am going to send it down (5:115) as munazziluhā, with the doubled letter.
### His words, Exalted: And when God said, "O Jesus" (5:116) — the verse.

Al-Tirmidhī — who declared it sound — al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Daylamī transmitted from Abū Hurayrah, who said: Jesus will put forward his argument, and it is God who will have put it into his mouth, in His words: And when God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?" (5:116). Abū Hurayrah said, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "So God put into his mouth: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to (5:116) — the whole verse."

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Maysarah, who said: When God said, And when God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?", every joint in him trembled until he fell down.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said: When He said, Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?, every joint of his shifted from its place out of fear.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah concerning His words Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?: when will that be? He said: On the Day of Resurrection. Do you not see that He says: This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:119)?

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words And when God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?": he said: When God raised Jesus son of Mary to Himself, the Christians said what they said, and claimed that Jesus had commanded them to do so. So He questioned him about his saying, and he said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say — up to His words — and You are witness over all things (5:116–117).

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Ṭāwūs concerning this verse: he said: Jesus and his Lord disputed in argument, and God granted him success, and so he said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to.

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted, by way of Ṭāwūs, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "Jesus's Lord argued with him, so Jesus argued with his Lord, and God put his argument into his mouth with His words: Did you say to the people — the verse."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the nations will be gathered, and every people will be called with their leader (imām)." He said: "And Jesus will be called, and He will say to Jesus: 'O Jesus, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God"?' And he will say: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to — up to His words — the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:116–119)."

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn Jurayj: And when God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?" — while the people were listening; and he answered Him with what you have seen, and acknowledged against himself his servanthood to Him, so that whoever used to say about Jesus what he used to say came to know that he had been speaking only falsehood.
Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words that you should worship God, my Lord and your Lord (5:117): he said: my Master and your Master.

Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them (5:117) — as long as I was among them."

Ibn Abī Shaybah, Aḥmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) delivered a sermon and said: "O people, you will be gathered to God barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." Then he recited: As We began the first creation, We shall repeat it — a promise binding upon Us; truly We shall do it (21:104). Then he said: "Truly, the first of created beings to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham. And truly, men of my community will be brought and taken off to the left side, and I shall say: 'O Lord, my companions, my companions!' And it will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' Then I shall say as the righteous servant said: And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me, You were the Watcher over them (5:117). And it will be said: 'As for these, they never ceased to turn back on their heels from the time you parted from them.'"
Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words You were the Watcher over them (5:117): he said: the Guardian.
ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from Qatādah concerning His words You were the Watcher: he said: the Guardian.
### His words, Exalted: If You punish them (5:118) — the verse.

Ibn Abī Shaybah in al-Muṣannaf, Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan transmitted from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed one night and recited a single verse until morning came, bowing with it and prostrating with it: If You punish them, they are Your servants (5:118) — the verse. When morning came I said: "O Messenger of God, you kept reciting this verse until morning came." He said: "I asked my Lord for intercession for my community, and He granted it to me; and it will reach, God willing, whoever does not associate anything with God."

Ibn Mājah transmitted from Abū Dharr, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) stood in prayer with a single verse until morning came, repeating it: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118).

Muslim, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ḥusn al-ẓann, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited the words of God concerning Abraham: My Lord, they have led astray many of the people; so whoever follows me is of me (14:36) — the verse; and the words of Jesus son of Mary: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: "O God, my community, my community!" and wept. So God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muḥammad and say: We shall satisfy you concerning your community, and We shall not grieve you."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) spent a night interceding for his community, and he kept praying with this verse: If You punish them, they are Your servants — to the end of the verse; with it he prostrated and with it he bowed, with it he stood and with it he sat, until morning came.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abū Dharr, who said: I said to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God! You stood tonight with a single verse of the Qurʾān, when you have the whole Qurʾān with you; had one of us done this, we would have held it against him." He said: "I prayed for my community." He said: "And what answer were you given?" He said: "I was given an answer such that, if many of them came to know of it, they would abandon the prayer." He said: "Shall I not give the people the good news?" He said: "Yes." Then ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of God, if you send this out to the people, they will slacken in worship." So he called out to him: "Come back!" and he came back; and he recited the verse that he had been reciting: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118).

Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: If You punish them, they are Your servants — he says: Your slaves, who have deserved punishment by their saying; and if You forgive them — that is, those of them whom You have left and whose lives have been prolonged until I am sent down from heaven to the earth to kill the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl), and they have withdrawn from their saying, declared You one, and acknowledged that we are servants; and if You forgive them, in that they have turned back from their saying, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise.

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words If You punish them, they are Your servants: he says: If You punish them — You make them die in their Christianity, so that the punishment becomes their due — they are Your servants; and if You forgive them — bringing them out of Christianity and guiding them to Islam — truly You are the Mighty, the Wise. This was the saying of Jesus (peace be upon him) in this world.
### His words, Exalted: God said (5:119) — the verse.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His words This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:119): he said: He says: This is the Day when those who affirm God's oneness will profit from their affirmation of His oneness.

Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted from al-Suddī concerning His words God said, "This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness": he said: This is a separate section from the speech of Jesus, and this is on the Day of Resurrection.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abū al-Shaykh transmitted from Qatādah, who said: Two speakers will speak on the Day of Resurrection: the prophet of God, Jesus, and Iblīs, the enemy of God. As for Iblīs, he will say: Truly God promised you a true promise — up to His words — except that I called you and you answered me (14:22); and the enemy of God will speak truly on that day, though in this world he was a liar. As for Jesus, it is what God has recounted to you in His words: And when God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?" (5:116) — to the end of the verse. Then God said: This is the Day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness; and he was truthful in the life of this world and after death.
### His words, Exalted: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens (5:120) — the verse.

Abū ʿUbayd in his Faḍāʾil transmitted from Abū al-Zāhiriyyah that ʿUthmān wrote at the end of al-Māʾidah: "To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing."{{fn:That is, with samīʿun baṣīr in place of the standard reading wa-huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr, "and He has power over all things".}}
### His words, Exalted: She said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you (19:18), and the following verses.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from Abū Wāʾil, concerning His words She said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), that he said: Mary knew that the God-fearing man is one who possesses restraint.

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Mujāhid, concerning His words She said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), that he said: She feared only that he wanted her for himself. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, that I may grant you a boy (19:19): they claimed that he breathed into the opening of her shift and into her sleeve.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd reported from ʿĀṣim that he read li-ahaba laki ("that I may grant you") with the hamzah written with alif, and that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh{{fn:ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, the Companion whose codex preserved a number of readings differing from the ʿUthmānic text.}} it is li-yahaba laki ("that He may grant you") with the yāʾ.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in the additions (Zawāʾid) to al-Zuhd, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, reported from Qatādah, concerning His words a pure boy (19:19), that he said: righteous.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His words nor have I been unchaste (19:20), that he said: a fornicatress.
Ibn Jarīr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words a distant place (19:22), that he said: far away.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from Mujāhid, concerning His words a distant place (19:22), that he said: remote. And concerning His words and the pangs of childbirth drove her (19:23), he said: compelled her.

Al-Ṭastī reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq{{fn:The Khārijite leader Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq, whose questions to Ibn ʿAbbās on rare Qurʾanic words, answered with citations of Arabic poetry, form a well-known collection.}} said to him: Tell me about His words, Mighty and Majestic, and the pangs of childbirth drove her (19:23). He said: compelled her. He said: And do the Arabs know that? He said: Yes; have you not heard Ḥassān ibn Thābit saying:
> When we made a true charge, we drove you to the foot of the mountain.
Ibn Abī Ḥātim reported from Qatādah, concerning His words and the pangs of childbirth drove her (19:23), that he said: forced her.
